questions.q: What makes Salesforce Connect fundamentally different from REST, SOAP, Bulk, and Composite?
options: It requires no authentication at all
It displays and queries data that lives in an external system live, via callout, without ever copying that data into Salesforce
It only works with the SOAP API, not REST
It is the fastest API for high-volume data loads
questions.explain: Every other API in this course assumes Salesforce stores its own copy of the data; Salesforce Connect's entire design is to avoid that copy, fetching data live from the external system on demand.

questions.q: What suffix identifies an external object's API name, parallel to __c for custom objects?
options: __ext
questions.explain: External objects use a __x suffix on their API name, distinguishing them from standard objects and __c custom objects.

questions.q: What happens behind the scenes when you run a SOQL query against an external object?
options: Salesforce makes a live callout to the external system to answer the query, rather than reading from its own stored database
The query always fails, since SOQL cannot target external objects
Salesforce silently copies the external data into its own database first
The query is converted into a Bulk API 2.0 job automatically
questions.explain: Even though the SOQL syntax looks identical to querying a normal object, Salesforce Connect answers it with a real-time callout to the external system rather than a local database read.

questions.q: What is the OData adapter option for Salesforce Connect?
options: A custom Apex class that must be written for every integration
A point-and-click, no-code configuration usable when the external system exposes an OData-compliant endpoint
A Bulk API 2.0 job type
A SOAP-only authentication mechanism
questions.explain: When the external system already speaks the OData protocol, the OData adapter lets an admin configure the connection without writing code.

questions.q: When would you need a custom Apex connector instead of the OData adapter for Salesforce Connect?
options: Whenever the external system does not expose an OData-compliant endpoint, requiring Apex code to translate requests and responses
Whenever the external system is also a Salesforce org
Custom Apex connectors are never needed; OData always works
Only when using the Bulk API instead of REST
questions.explain: The Apex Connector Framework exists specifically for external systems that don't speak OData, requiring custom code to bridge Salesforce Connect's requests to that system's actual API.
